chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The resident of Makkah, when he enters it for Umrah during the months other than the Hajj months — in Rajab or Sha'ban or the month of Ramadan or any other of the months except the Hajj months, for indeed the Hajj months are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijjah — whoever enters it for Umrah during the months other than the Hajj months, then intends to enter the state of Ihram, let him go out to Al-Ji'ranah and enter Ihram from there.

Then he should come to Makkah and not break the Talbiyah until he looks at the House. Then he should circumambulate the House and pray two Rak'at at the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Then he should go out to As-Safa and Al-Marwa and circumambulate between them. Then he should shorten (his hair/nails) and free himself (from Ihram). Then he should renew the Talbiyah on the Day of Tarwiyah.

key_terms.أَشْهُرُ الْحَجِّ: The months of Hajj (Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَ الْمَرْوَةِ: As-Safa and Al-Marwa (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.الْجِعْرَانَةِ: Al-Ji'ranah, a specific boundary place near Makkah
key_terms.يَحِلُّ: Frees himself (from the state of Ihram)
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: Enters the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: Shortens (hair/nails), indicating the end of Umrah Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the correct ritual procedure for a resident of Makkah performing Umrah in non-Hajj months according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the ritual protocol for the residents of Mecca (Ahl al-Qar) performing Umrah during non-Hajj months, requiring them to exit to the boundary of Al-Ji'ranah to assume Ihram before re-entering. It highlights the distinct Shia practice of renewing the Talbiyah on the Day of Tarwiyah (8th Dhu al-Hijjah) to transition from Umrah to Hajj, emphasizing the continuity of ritual state. This procedure underscores the scholarly emphasis on precise geographical boundaries and the temporal separation of Umrah and Hajj rites for local residents.
